business_problem: The Austrian Armed Forces needed a trustworthy way to query large volumes of open-source and internal documentation because users required fact-based answers with traceable sources, low hallucination risk, and human oversight.
solution_summary: IBM Austria and the Federal Ministry for National Defence created ChatZentDoc as a minimal viable product for trusted generative AI over defense documentation. The ministry already used IBM Watson Explorer for natural-language processing and data collection, so IBM Client Engineering extended that foundation with IBM watsonx.ai to add source-grounded answer generation. The resulting front end lets users query the knowledge base in natural language, filter results, and export answers together with the cited source documents. The system also refreshes its information daily and includes a feedback loop so the ZentDok team can continuously improve response quality. By combining legacy NLP assets with newer generative AI under a human-in-the-loop operating model, the ministry built an OSINT-style knowledge service that supports defense analysts without relinquishing transparency or legal control.

solution_components.role: Adds fact-based response generation over the defense knowledge base.

data_flow: Daily-updated source documents flow into the ZentDok knowledge base, Watson Explorer and watsonx.ai process the content for retrieval and answer generation, and ChatZentDoc returns filterable, exportable responses with cited sources for user review.
business_outcome: The ministry gained a trusted AI interface for evidence-backed information retrieval while preserving human review, source traceability, and alignment with public-sector security requirements.
architecture_clues: Responses are grounded in cited source documents that can be exported with the answer.
The knowledge base is updated daily to preserve timeliness for defense use cases.
The operating model is explicitly human-in-the-loop and designed to minimize hallucination risk.
